applicationInfo.name: tdd
applicationInfo.description: Threat Driven Development: a Claude Code plugin, git hooks, a CLI and a GitHub Action that require every merge to main to carry a Threat Composer threat model delta or a justified no-threat-delta declaration.

architecture.description: Components: (1) the tdd CLI (Python, stdlib only) that parses Threat Composer files, computes semantic deltas, evaluates declarations and runs named checks; (2) a Claude Code plugin whose SessionStart, PostToolUse and Stop hooks call the CLI; (3) git commit-msg and pre-push hooks that call the CLI; (4) a composite GitHub Action that runs `tdd ci` on pull requests.

dataflow.description: Inputs: repository files and git history, .tdd/config.json, .tc.json models, commit messages, and the pull request body (CI only). Outputs: pass/fail exit codes, hook JSON to Claude Code, and a markdown job summary. Check commands from .tdd/config.json run as shell in CI and on explicit local request.

assumptions.content: Branch protection on main requires the threat-gate job to pass and disallows direct pushes.

mitigations.content: tdd lint and tdd validate check models against the vendored official Threat Composer JSON Schema and the editor's own stricter rules, in hooks and in CI.
A threat is resolved only under exactly one risk strategy tag; accept, transfer and avoid require a written reason. Lint, status and CI treat anything else as red.

A mitigation is resolved exactly when its checks pass: tdd check --resolve flips it in the same change as the implementation, and CI fails on a lagging status or a resolved mitigation whose check fails.

tdd writes models in the exact form the Threat Composer editor saves, keeps angle-bracket tags as curly braces instead of letting the editor delete them, refuses text it would escape, reformats agent edits in the PostToolUse hook, and CI fails on unformatted models.
Only semantic changes (threats, mitigations, assumptions, links) count as a delta; formatting and renumbering do not.
The GitHub Action runs tdd ci on every pull request with full history, so skipping local hooks does not skip the gate.
Claude Code hooks never execute checks; they read only cached results. Checks run only on explicit tdd check/status --run-checks/ci.
Mitigations reference checks by name with a check: tag followed by the check name; commands live only in .tdd/config.json, which is itself gated.
Declarations must meet a minimum length and are rejected when they match a boilerplate list.
tdd ci reads policy from the base branch; config changes take effect only after merge. Check definitions come from head.
The action passes the PR body and refs to its script through env vars and never interpolates ${{ }} expressions inside run: blocks.

threats.prerequisites: who edits a threat model by hand or with an agent
threats.threatAction: commit a file that the Threat Composer editor refuses to open
threats.threatImpact: a threat model nobody can review in the editor
threats.statement: A contributor who edits a threat model by hand or with an agent can commit a file that the Threat Composer editor refuses to open, which leads to a threat model nobody can review in the editor, resulting in reduced availability of threat model

threats.prerequisites: with edit access to the threat model
threats.threatAction: mark a threat resolved without recording whether its risk was mitigated, accepted, transferred or avoided
threats.threatImpact: unowned residual risk that reviewers assume is mitigated
threats.statement: A contributor with edit access to the threat model can mark a threat resolved without recording whether its risk was mitigated, accepted, transferred or avoided, which leads to unowned residual risk that reviewers assume is mitigated, resulting in reduced integrity of threat model

threats.threatAction: mark a mitigation resolved that was never implemented, or leave an implemented one marked identified
threats.threatImpact: reviewers trusting a threat model that misstates what is actually mitigated
threats.statement: A contributor who edits the threat model can mark a mitigation resolved that was never implemented, or leave an implemented one marked identified, which leads to reviewers trusting a threat model that misstates what is actually mitigated, resulting in reduced integrity of threat model

threats.prerequisites: who opens a threat model in the Threat Composer VS Code editor
threats.threatAction: cause the editor to silently rewrite the file, stripping angle-bracket text and reordering keys
threats.threatImpact: lost threat model content and noisy diffs that hide real changes
threats.statement: A reviewer who opens a threat model in the Threat Composer VS Code editor can cause the editor to silently rewrite the file, stripping angle-bracket text and reordering keys, which leads to lost threat model content and noisy diffs that hide real changes, resulting in reduced integrity of threat model

threats.prerequisites: that is blocked by the Stop hook
threats.threatAction: write a vague declaration or reformat the threat model to satisfy the gate
threats.statement: A coding agent that is blocked by the Stop hook can write a vague declaration or reformat the threat model to satisfy the gate, which leads to unreviewed attack surface reaching main, resulting in reduced integrity of threat review process

threats.prerequisites: who pushes with --no-verify or without the hooks installed
threats.threatAction: merge code that carries no threat delta or declaration
threats.statement: A developer who pushes with --no-verify or without the hooks installed can merge code that carries no threat delta or declaration, which leads to unreviewed attack surface reaching main, resulting in reduced integrity of threat review process

threats.prerequisites: that a developer opens with the plugin installed
threats.threatAction: define check commands that the Claude Code hooks run automatically
threats.threatImpact: code execution on the developer workstation
threats.statement: A malicious repository that a developer opens with the plugin installed can define check commands that the Claude Code hooks run automatically, which leads to code execution on the developer workstation, resulting in reduced confidentiality and/or integrity of developer workstation

threats.threatAction: embed shell commands that CI runs as a check
threats.statement: A threat model author who can edit a .tc.json file can embed shell commands that CI runs as a check, which leads to arbitrary code execution in CI, resulting in reduced integrity of CI runner

threats.prerequisites: who wants to skip threat review
threats.statement: A contributor who wants to skip threat review can submit a boilerplate no-threat-delta declaration, which leads to unreviewed attack surface reaching main, resulting in reduced integrity of threat review process

threats.prerequisites: who can open a pull request
threats.threatAction: weaken .tdd/config.json policy in the same change it is gated on
threats.threatImpact: code merging without a threat review
threats.statement: A contributor who can open a pull request can weaken .tdd/config.json policy in the same change it is gated on, which leads to code merging without a threat review, resulting in reduced integrity of threat review process

threats.prerequisites: who can edit the PR title or description
threats.threatAction: inject shell syntax that the gate's workflow step evaluates
threats.threatImpact: arbitrary code execution in CI with the workflow token
threats.statement: A pull request author who can edit the PR title or description can inject shell syntax that the gate's workflow step evaluates, which leads to arbitrary code execution in CI with the workflow token, resulting in reduced integrity and/or confidentiality of CI runner and repository token
